lessons.rule:
Main-hand levels are the second engine (+6 levels is about +1.3 blinds).
- Choose the main hand by how often you can draw it with 2 discards: you should be able to draw it in 3 of 4 hands. How often you have played it does not decide the choice, unless you own Telescope (its pack planet goes to your most played hand). But your levels must match the hand the round player really plays. If by ante 2 it mostly plays a different drawable hand (Two Pair played 5 times while Pair was 'the plan'), do one of two things: lock the style to the main hand, or level the hand it is playing (Uranus counts). Doing neither is the failure. Never flip the style back and forth between Pair and Two Pair.
- Pair is the default once the board has +Mult or chips jokers. It is always drawable, and Sly, Jolly, Duo, Half Joker and Mercury support it. On a blank board (no jokers), Pair is not the plan; see the in-blind pace rule. Leave Pair only for a real signal: Spare Trousers, or a hand-type joker plus a steady supply of that hand's planets. A single common +Mult joker (a $4 Mad Joker, even a free one from a tag) is not a signal, and one off-plan planet from a pack is not a signal either.
- Use Full House, Straight or Flush only with a real enabler.
- Commit by the end of ante 1-2 (by the first Buffoon pick at the latest), and make sure the round player actually plays that hand. Once the main hand is named, buy only its planets and jokers that score it. Do not let a joker (e.g. Runner) pull plays toward Straights, or spread plays over Full House, Two Pair and High Card. If the jokers you own really support a different hand, switch to that hand by ante 3 at the latest and stop buying the old hand's planets. Pair levelled but played 0 times by ante 4, while Clever, Uranus and Earth were bought for other hands, was a failure.
- Take every planet for the main hand (Mercury whenever it is offered). Do not spend money on off-plan planets. Exception: when a pack you already opened (free or paid) has no main-hand planet, take the planet for a related hand (Two Pair, Three of a Kind, Full House; not Pluto) rather than nothing. That insures you against The Eye and The Mouth. Count that pack as a miss, not as progress, and never as a reason to open another pack. Three Plutos took High Card to level 4, and it was played 4 times.
- Targets: level 2-3 by the ante 2 boss (buy at least one main-hand planet before it), 3-5 by antes 3-4, 6-9 by antes 5-6. Never let a second ante pass with the main hand at level 1. Runs that bought no planet in 16 decisions, or played Pair 19 times at level 1 into ante 4, died. Once the hand is at target, planets stop counting as progress. Send the surplus toward xMult instead. While the board has no reliable xMult, do not keep building planet infrastructure for a hand already at target: $38 of Telescope and packs took Pair to level 8 while the outlook still showed a cliff.
- While below target: buy the main-hand planet on sight ($3-4). Take one Celestial look per shop before any joker reroll, and always buy the planet before a 2nd reroll in the same shop. When the hand is 2+ levels below target, single planets, Celestial packs ($4) and Telescope all come before rerolls. One Celestial look is too little then: $18 went to rerolls at $48 with only two packs opened all run, and Pair started ante 5 at level 2. On a thin board under $10, a $3-4 planet beats a reroll or a second Buffoon pack. Cap rerolls at about $10 per ante unless you hold $60+. Below level 3 at ante 3, or below level 4 at ante 4, planets also come before holding interest above $25. Below about $15 with no way to reach $25 within the next ante, interest is worth only $1-2 a round, so do not pass Telescope, a Celestial pack or Mercury to protect a tier. Passing them at $11-13 left Pair at level 1 into ante 4 and at level 3 at ante 6. Take a Meteor Tag when it comes free, but do not skip a blind in antes 2-4 just for one, because the shop you give up could show an xMult.
- Reroll budget: if $10 of rerolls in one ante has not found an xMult, put the rest of the surplus into main-hand planets (single planets, Celestial packs) until the hand reaches target. Levels are certain progress; rerolls are a lottery.
- Celestial packs: buy them only to level the main hand. Once the main-hand planet shows up in shops, buy it there for $3 rather than chasing it through packs (6 packs for $26 gave only 2 Mercury; 5 packs for $24 gave only 2). While below target, open a Celestial pack if you keep $20+ after it, or about $10-15 once $25 is covered, and nothing better is on offer. A voucher that fixes the run (Director's Cut) always comes first. Prefer packs to rerolls and to $6+ flat jokers and slow scalers. Buy Normal packs, not Mega, unless 2+ planets in the Mega pack are on-plan. Do not pass packs because 'Mercury is only 25%'. Never open one that leaves you unable to fix the coming blind.
- If the main hand's planets have not shown up after two antes (by ante 3), switch to a drawable hand whose planets you keep being offered. If Pair jokers are on the board, that means Pair: buy the Mercury you were turning down. If packs have already levelled another drawable hand while the main hand sits at level 1, set the style to that hand so the levels get used. Venus and Uranus took Three of a Kind and Two Pair to level 2, but the style stayed on Pair and those levels were never played.
- Telescope and Planet Merchant pay off only when about 3+ Celestial packs will follow them, or with Constellation. When that is the plan and the main hand is committed, buy Telescope in antes 2-4 even if it costs one interest tier. Passing it at ante 2 as 'off-plan' led to packs that gave only off-plan planets. Do not buy it for a hand already at target while the board still lacks xMult. Below target with no pack plan, spend that $10 on direct main-hand planets first.

In antes 1-2, survival beats interest until two conditions hold: the board has 2 lasting, unconditional scoring jokers (+Mult or chips that fire on ordinary hands), and the main hand is level 2 or higher. Survival means every blind of the current ante, including its boss: treat a boss reading below about 85% as a failing blind, even if the next blind reads 97%. When the current blind already reads 95%+ and the boss is safe too, do not pay for perishable, decaying or off-plan jokers, packs or rerolls. Until those 2 scorers are in place:
- Do not leave a shop holding $15+ while a blind of this ante is failing. Spend down to about $10. In ante 1, go below $10 only if a blind of this ante would fail, or if the next ante's Small Blind already reads below about 30%. In that case buy direct scorers or main-hand planets down to about $5-8; rerolls stay under the reroll rule's floors. Never finish ante 1 under $10 otherwise. Ending ante 1 near $0 wipes out the Yellow Deck head start, and those runs never reached $25.
- Take a joker that scores now over a scaler that starts at 0 (e.g. Red Card), even if the scorer is a rental (see the rentals rule).
- An early conditional xMult (The Idol, The Duo) is a finisher, not a base. Until there is one unconditional +Mult or chips joker or a levelled main hand, rank cheap unconditional scorers and main-hand planets above conditional or perishable jokers. A board of only conditional (Crafty, Idol) and expiring (Sly, Duo) jokers had nothing left by ante 2.
- Cheap +Mult stopgaps (Jolly, Raised Fist, Gros Michel, or any joker with a perishable sticker) are a bridge only when the current blind fails without them. Otherwise take a non-perishable scorer even if it is slightly weaker. Never let two stopgaps expire in the same ante or right at a boss.
- Use the Yellow Deck head start on Buffoon packs only as part of a plan to reach $25 by ante 3. The extra $10 pays for one early pack, not for a pack plus a reroll plus a buy. In ante 1, open one only if you could still afford a shop joker or a reroll after a miss. If the pack misses and the shop has no scorer, keep the cash for the next shop.
- Every joker slot and pack pick goes to scoring. Do not take utility or economy jokers (Drunkard, Chaos, Splash, Mail-In Rebate, To the Moon, Cloud 9, Certificate, or Sixth Sense bought only to feed Swashbuckler's sell value) or a $10 voucher like Grabber. In antes 1-2 a Buffoon pack with no scorer is a skip, so take nothing rather than a free non-scorer. A free Drunkard left one real scorer going into a 10% Flint. It set off a reroll and rental chain, and later Banner depended on it.
- Zero scoring jokers before any blind from the ante 1 Big Blind on is an emergency. Buy any affordable scorer. If there is none, do one $5 reroll, then open an Arcana pack (Judgement). Never enter a blind with an empty board while holding $10+.
- With no scoring jokers, play for the biggest base hand you can draw (see the in-blind pace rule) and take pack jokers that pay off now (Runner over Certificate).
- An early xMult (e.g. Card Sharp) must be followed at once by an unconditional base joker and a main-hand planet.
- Take a value generator only when the next boss is safe by the conservative check.
Once the 2 lasting scorers are in place, bank: aim for $25 by the end of ante 2, and hold $25 from ante 3.

Reroll limits:
- At most 2 rerolls per shop, and only 1 in an ante the outlook shows as safe. Spread them across shops. Never chain escalating rerolls ($5, $6, $7, $8) in one shop ($44 to $26 right after a Hermit windfall found nothing). Pay for a joker on offer rather than for more looks at the shop.
- Set your buy bar before you reroll. If two rerolls in a row show only cheap scorers you pass on, the bar is too high: lower it and buy the best scorer instead of rerolling again. In one run, nine rerolls ($51 over antes 3-4) bought no joker, and the last money went to random tarots.
- Never reroll if you could not then buy a $6-8 xMult on top of your floor. One run noted 'at $13 I can't buy an xMult after a reroll' and then rerolled from $7 to $2. If two or three shops in a row turn up nothing, stop rerolling. Put the surplus into main-hand planets or rebuild money so the xMult can be bought when it appears.
- Antes 1-2: never reroll when it takes money below about $15. While one or two shops remain before the boss, do not reroll below $20 either. A low boss read early in the ante is not yet an emergency, so buy the cheap scorer on offer now. $21→$10 of rerolls found nothing, then the natural shops' Lusty and Ice Cream took a 10% Flint to 100%. A self-declared 'thin-board exception' does not override this; put thin-board money into a direct scorer or a main-hand planet instead. Rerolls at $14→$9, $13→$8 and $12→$7 all found nothing and left later shops unable to buy a $4 pack. When the current ante reads 95-100%, do not reroll below $25: $5 rerolls at $21 and $20 on safe antes found nothing while Pair stayed level 1. The only allowed exception is a single emergency reroll on an empty board before a blind; never chain a second one. Leave ante 1 with $10-15 so the ante 2 shops can buy two scorers.
- With a rental, keep at least rent + $4 after any reroll, so the next shop can still buy a Celestial pack, a planet or a cheap +Mult joker.
- In antes 1-2, never spend $15+ rerolling one shop.
- In a safe ante, do not reroll if it drops you below the next $5 interest tier.
- Once 2 lasting scorers exist, never reroll below $20 unless the NEXT blind or the current ante's boss reads below 70%. While every blind of the current ante reads 95%+, never reroll below $25 ($28 with a rental), whatever the forecast for later antes says. The severe-forecast exception releases money for planets, Buffoon packs and empty-slot scorers, not for rerolls. Runs that used it to reroll at 95-100% antes spent about $50 on 9-10 rerolls each and found no xMult. Buy the certain upgrades (main-hand planet, Celestial or Buffoon pack) before any reroll.
- If the main hand is below its level target, take a Celestial look first and cap rerolls at about $10 per ante. If $10 of rerolls in one ante has found no xMult, stop and put the surplus into main-hand planets.
- Buy money-scaling jokers (Bull, Bootstraps) only if you will really hold $25+. Do not buy them on a plan that spends heavily on rerolls or rentals, or while the engine is still being bought. A core Bootstraps made the strategist refuse a boss counter, and the run lost to The Club. While you own one, check the next-blind outlook after each spend. Stop if it would fall below about 85% or drop more than 5 points. Spending that breaks the next blind while chasing a later one is not survival.
- From ante 3, reroll only with money above $25 ($28 with a rental, $31 with two), and only if you can open a slot: know which joker you would sell before you reroll. Below $20 at ante 3+, do not reroll at all unless the next blind reads below 70% (rerolling $15 to $10 to $5 at ante 4 left $2 at ante 5; $17 to $6 at ante 5 left $2-5 for the next two shops).
- Stop once one shop has used about $20 on rerolls. Never pay $8-10 for a reroll unless you hold $60+.
Never rerolling at all is also a failure. While the board has fewer than 2 multipliers, use 1-2 $5 rerolls per shop with money above the floor, in the early shops of the ante rather than the boss shop. If the boss itself is the problem, first look for a fix aimed at that boss (Director's Cut, glass from Justice, a skip that avoids it).

Rentals and debt. A rental's real price is $3 times the rounds you will keep it (about 20 rounds from ante 2, so about $15-20+ even for a $1 rental), not its sticker. Compare that with a Celestial pack plus a reroll. A rental also raises the money floor to $28, which blocks rerolls for the rest of the run.
Ante 1: buy no rentals, even at $1, unless the current blind fails without one. The other exceptions:
- The board has no scoring joker and either the ante's boss reads below about 90% or ante 2's Small Blind reads below about 50%. Then a rental that scores now (e.g. Half Joker on Pair) beats a scaler that starts at 0. Yellow Deck can carry one rental.
- You hold an xMult with no base. Then a big flat-chips rental (Stuntman +250) or an affordable Bootstraps is worth it.
Ante 2: buy a rental only if the current blind reads below about 50% and no non-rental option fixes it, or under the lasting-scaler exception below. Antes 3-4: buy one only if the next blind reads below 70% without it, or under one of the exceptions. Carry at most one rental in antes 2-4. Rentals stacked one per ante (Ice Cream at ante 1, Acrobat, then an eternal Half Joker) pushed rent to $9 a round and money from $21 to $3. A flat scoring rental (Raised Fist, Banner, a late Green Joker; Seltzer is a retrigger, not +Mult) bought while the ante reads 90%+ is never worth it. Never take a rental for flat Mult when a non-rental fix exists, such as Director's Cut for a bad boss. Never take a money-scaling rental (Bull) in antes 1-4 unless you will really keep $28+, even when it is free from a pack. Rent plus spending down makes it weaker every round (Bull ended at +10 chips on $5). From ante 3, one lasting rental that is a core scorer for the main hand (Hanging Chad, Even Steven on an even-heavy deck) is acceptable only with a free slot and only if you still hold $28 after buying it. Never take a new rental below $20. If a second rental is the only survival fix, sell one at the first shop where the next blind reads 85%+ without it. Never hold two rentals below $28, and never carry two across an ante below $31.
Lasting-scaler exception (Yellow Deck): from ante 2, with $25+ in hand and the next boss safe, one rental that is a lasting xMult or a scaler you will really feed (Hologram; Green Joker played with zero discards) is acceptable even though the blind does not need it. Hold $28 afterwards. A growing $3-a-round rental beats a chain of perishables replaced every 5 rounds; passing Green Joker and Hologram for their sticker led to far more spent on perishables and rerolls.
xMult exception: from ante 2, if the board has no xMult and an upcoming boss reads below 50%, an affordable rental xMult that fires on every main-hand play (Cavendish, Card Sharp on a repeated hand, Baseball with Uncommons, Acrobat, Vampire) beats any flat +Mult option. Accept an eternal rental only for such an every-hand xMult when nothing sellable is available. Never use the exception for a periodic or conditional xMult (Loyalty Card fires about once in 6 hands; The Order on an uncommitted hand). Refuse it too if you already carry a rental.
Eternal rentals: never buy one for anything except that every-hand xMult. It cannot be sold, so it charges $3 every round for the rest of the run. A $1 eternal rental Banner (Wheel 15%→85%) kept money at $1-17 for the rest of the run, blocked a $4 Hanging Chad at $2, and tied the board to Drunkard. An eternal rental Half Joker bought at $22 did the same and locked a slot to flat Mult. If only a rental saves a blind, first check a main-hand planet or a pack, then use a plain rental you can sell.
Always:
- With a rental, the floor is $28, not $25. Never spend to $0 while holding one: the fee puts you into debt and locks you out of the next shops.
- Never use Credit Card or debt to pay for scoring in antes 1-3. At $0 or below, buy no rentals.
- Never take a rental that is perishable or decaying (Popcorn, Ice Cream, Ramen). Never carry a third rental.
- Sell a survival rental as soon as the blind you rented it for is behind you, unless the outlook shows you still need it. Sell it before any other joker once a non-rental scorer can replace it, or once the next blind is 90%+ safe without it. Do not keep a shrinking rental (an Ice Cream rental kept from 100 down to 15 chips).
- Do not let the $28/$31 floor block buys that improve the build.
- Before a boss that costs money (The Tooth, $1 per card), enter with cash for the cards you expect to play + $3 per rental + $5. Play 4-card hands or as few hands as possible.

Interest against forecasts (once 2 lasting scorers exist; before that, the survival rule applies). Hold $25 only once the board already passes the next ante. Drop below $25 ($28 with a rental) for survival only when the next blind or the current ante's boss reads below about 70%. In antes 2-5 the forecast for the NEXT ante, read off the current board, is almost always bad. On its own it never justifies spending down every ante or rerolling below $25. Runs that treated it as an emergency at 95-100% antes went $34→$9, $37→$7 and $29→$18 on rerolls and found no xMult. A high outlook that rests on a variable joker (Ancient, Idol, Castle), or a boss that hides information, is no reason to spend the bank either. From ante 4, while the current ante reads 95%+, spend only the surplus above $25 ($28 with a rental) and never drop below $20, so ante 5 can still buy a fix. A reroll plus a Mega Celestial at 99%/95% took $29 to $17, and ante 5 then opened at $20 against a 0% boss and stayed broke for three antes.
Severe-forecast exception, which applies especially with no xMult. A cliff one ante away is an emergency now, not when you reach it, but it releases money only for certain upgrades, never for extra rerolls:
- Next ante's boss below about 50%: spend down to the $25 tier in every shop of the current ante.
- Next ante's boss or Big Blind below about 30%, any blind of the next ante below about 20%, or the board's only xMult is perishable and expires within the next ante: the interest floor no longer applies to certain upgrades. Add at least one in each shop of the current ante, even at the cost of an interest tier: a main-hand planet, a Celestial pack while below target, a Buffoon pack, or a scorer for the played hand in an empty slot. If the main hand is 3+ levels below target, related-hand planets and Planet Merchant count too. Spend down to about $15 plus $3 per rental, and no lower, so the cliff ante still has money. Runs that left shops at $11-20 while the next ante read 0-10% passed Uranus, Mars and Square Joker to protect a floor. They then spent $18 in the dying ante's first shop, or paid $8 for a Mega pack to get the same planet. Runs that entered the cliff ante at $9-13 could not reroll in the ante that killed them.
- Rerolls under the exception: while every blind of the current ante reads 95%+, reroll only with money above $25 (at most 2 per shop), and only after the certain upgrades are bought. If the outlook has shown the next ante at 0-10% for two antes in a row, the build lacks a multiplier, and planets and perishables will not fix it. Start $5 xMult rerolls and Buffoon packs from that surplus. If three shops in a row miss, stop rerolling and rebuild to the price of an xMult ($6-10) so you can buy it when it appears.
Act in the current ante's shops that still have a blind after them, while rerolls still cost $5. Do not save the money for the dying ante: arriving there and spending $28 down to $7 with only 1-2 shops left found nothing. Spend only on things that directly add xMult, main-hand levels or, in an empty slot, score on the played hand. Spectral and random Arcana packs and one-card tarots do not count as fixing a forecast. The exception is an Arcana aimed at a named edit on trigger cards (glass or steel). $30 down to $9 on a Spectral and an Arcana Jumbo added no multiplier. Do not dump the money into escalating rerolls in one shop.
When the boss is below 50% and you dip into survival money, judge each $ by how much it raises the boss estimate. Prefer a main-hand planet already in the shop, then joker rerolls. If two buys in a row miss, stop and keep the interest.

Unreliable scoring is backup, not the plan. That includes perishable jokers, decaying ones (Ice Cream, Popcorn, Seltzer, Turtle Bean), random ones (Misprint), time-limited ones (Seltzer, 10 hands; Ramen) and destroyable ones (Gros Michel, 1 in 6).
- Count a perishable as a scorer only for the blinds it will still be alive for, which usually means the current ante. Count its remaining rounds against the first blind the outlook marks as failing. If it expires before that blind, the problem is not solved: keep searching for a permanent xMult at the same priority and keep money ready for it. A perishable Duo or Blueprint does not cover the multiplier gap.
- When a perishable xMult is the board's main multiplier, count its rounds on the day you take it. Plan its replacement to arrive at least one shop before expiry: either a lasting xMult, or enough main-hand levels that the next ante's Big Blind reads 50%+ without it. Never 'keep interest' while a perishable carries the board. A Duo with 5 rounds left was noted to expire in ante 5 at four shops in a row while $20 was banked; it expired and the read fell to 12%.
- Hold at most 2 perishables at once. Once 2 are on the board, the next joker bought must be a lasting one, even if it scores less now. Never replace an expiring perishable with another perishable, or sell a lasting scorer to buy one, unless the current blind fails without it. Boards that chained five perishables (selling a permanent +4 Joker for a perishable Splash) spent antes 3-4 swapping out expiring jokers. Each fix expired just as the cliff arrived.
- When checking a boss two or more blinds ahead, count a decaying joker at what it will be worth by then (often near zero) and a perishable that expires first as zero. By ante 3, have at least 2 scoring jokers that do not shrink. One board leaned on Ice Cream (100 to 50 chips), Popcorn (20 to 4 Mult) and a perishable Zany. Each fix covered only the current ante, and ante 3-4 read 0%. If a bridge is the only fix, buy it, but the next spend goes to something lasting, not another bridge.
- Do not pay $5 for a shrinking joker when it leaves you under $5, unless the current blind fails without it. A 100-chip Ice Cream bought at a 97-100% read was down to 75 chips by ante 2, and the round player had to play around it.
- Never let two perishables expire in the same ante or right at a boss.
- When the danger is 1-2 antes out and the current ante reads 80%+, two cases apply. Both rules have support.
  (a) Do not churn stopgaps. Stopgaps bought and sold one shop later drained $50 to $18 and left nothing for the second xMult. A rental Wily and a perishable Golden Joker bought as patches had the same result. Do not let stopgaps take the money or slot meant for xMult, main-hand planets or deck shaping, and do not skip for packs that only offer perishables.
  (b) With an empty slot and the next ante below about 30%, do not turn down a joker that scores on the played hand only because of its sticker, within the 2-perishable cap. That covers perishable, eternal (see the eternal rule) and one rental if none is held. Buy it if it will still be alive at the failing blind: a 5-round perishable bought in the ante before covers the whole danger ante. Turning down Ride the Bus, Smiley, Blue Joker, Supernova, Bull and others for their stickers while 2-3 slots sat empty and $50 went into empty rerolls lost the run. So did keeping the 'lasting pieces only' filter from ante 2.
- Replace a shrinking chips joker before it falls to about half its value (Ice Cream below about 75 chips).
- From ante 3, treat a flat joker that scores under 10% of the hand as a slot to free. Sell it as soon as the shop offers anything better for the main hand.
- If more than half the board's scoring is unreliable, work out the bad case: Gros Michel gone, Misprint at about +5, decay after 4 more hands. Keep buying lasting scoring until the boss clears without those pieces.
- Never let a perishable or rental joker be your only chips source.

Judge a board by its reliable scoring. The outlook is simulated with the boss's effect and the build as it is, but it still averages over lucky draws, and it can glitch.
- When reaching the target depends on a conditional joker (suit, rank or hand-type jokers, Flower Pot, Idol, Ancient, Castle) or on unreliable pieces, treat the boss as less safe than shown. If the whole board is one conditional joker (e.g. Wrathful, which fires on 13 of 52 cards), read 95% as about 85% for skip, reroll and leave-shop decisions. Lower it further when the boss debuffs cards or cuts hand options (The Head, The Goad, The Club against a face-card board of Smiley and Scary Face).
- Before the boss, plan on the lowest recent read for that boss in the ante, not the latest one. If any read this ante was below about 75%, spend in the last shop on something that counters the boss, even at the cost of an interest tier. Do not let a money-scaling joker (Bootstraps) talk you out of it. The Club read 50/65/75/85/92% across the ante; the strategist left the last shop on the 92% read, turned down Judgement to protect Bootstraps, and lost the round at 48%.
- Do not trust a high outlook on an empty board. With zero jokers and every hand at level 1, even a 300-chip Small Blind rated 98% has been lost. Play it by the in-blind pace rule, not as already won. Treat any blind of 450 or more as below 80%, whatever the simulator says. If a jokerless blind falls behind (a weak first hand), drop all shop planning and play only for the chip target.
- Check a reading that jumps or drops with no change to the board or the blind before acting on it, especially one you already flagged as an artifact. Query it again, or compare it with the round player's clear estimate. Never let an unchecked low reading trigger 'survival overrides interest' and a full spend: a suspect 12% on The Wheel drove $17 to $0, and the round player then put The Wheel at about 100%.
- Before each ante step (especially 3 to 4, which is x2.8), check that the next ante's Small Blind is not already below 70% in the outlook. If it is, keep buying lasting scoring even if it costs an interest tier.

Buy only jokers that fire on what you actually play and own. Before turning a joker down, check its condition against the main hand.
- Fix the main hand (Pair by default) by the first Buffoon pick. From then on, buy only scorers for that hand or unconditional ones. No jokers for a different hand type (Droll/Crafty for Flush, Crazy or Devious for Straight, Zany for Three of a Kind, Clever for Two Pair on a Pair plan) as a bridge or as filler, and never as an Eternal 'because it is the only scorer on offer'. An Eternal Crafty bought next to Sly and Duo left Flush and Pair jokers that never fired together, and every hand stayed level 1. A Clever Joker bought on a Pair plan split the run between Pair, Two Pair, Full House and Straight. Buy unconditional +Mult or chips instead (Abstract, Banner, Popcorn; Jolly and Half Joker when Pair is the main hand, since a 2-card Pair always meets '3 or fewer cards'), or reroll to find one. Not Blackboard, a conditional xMult that needs held Spades/Clubs.
- This applies to conditional xMult too. Do not buy The Order, The Tribe, The Family and similar for a hand you are not committed to, or cannot draw reliably (a Straight with no Shortcut or Four Fingers). This matters even more when the buy drops you below $10. An $8 Order on a Pair board was dead weight, and selling it raised the boss read.
- Jokers tied to face cards or ranks (Photograph, Scary Face) fire only on some Pairs, so they are weaker than they look. No jokers that need cards you lack (Stone Joker with no Stone cards). Early on, skip conditional support (Mime without a strong held-in-hand card).
- Early on, buy jokers that scale, multiply or add plain +Mult. Prefer one that scores now over a scaler starting at 0. If the shop has none, keep the money rather than filling slots with conditional or off-hand jokers.
- Buy for the smaller side. Before buying a scorer, multiply it out: score ≈ (hand chips + joker chips) × (hand mult + joker mult) × xMult. If chips are already about 10 times mult or more (e.g. 100+ chips against Pair's x2-3), the next buy must be +Mult or xMult. Pass on chip jokers then, unless nothing else is offered and the next blind fails without one. Ice Cream plus Sly gave about 160 chips against x3; Sly lifted The Fish only from 10% to 15%, and a +4 Mult joker would have added about 2.5 times as much. Likewise, once Mult is above about 30 and chips are under about 100, another +Mult is nearly worthless. Buy chips (main-hand planets, Stuntman, Hiker, Blue Joker, Square, Ice Cream, Bull) or xMult instead, and skip flat +Mult even when it is free. From ante 5, a board with 2+ +Mult jokers and an xMult but no chips joker, scoring under about 200 chips on the main hand, ranks a lasting chips source (Castle, Stuntman, Bull, Hiker, Blue Joker, Arrowhead, Odd Todd or Scholar for Pair) above another +Mult or planet. Look for it with the ante 5-6 surplus, not in ante 7.
- If you keep a scaler with a trigger you control, feed it on purpose: for Red Card, skip cheap packs whose contents are worth less than +3 Mult, but from ante 3 only with money that stays at $25+. Below $25, open a pack only if it could hold the main-hand planet or an xMult joker. Every $5 below $25 costs $1 a round, and feeding Red Card took $34 to $11 and kept antes 3-4 at $7-15. If you won't feed it, don't keep it while you lack scoring.
- No sideways swaps. Do not sell a flat or conditional joker to buy another of the same kind. From ante 3, do not buy flat or perishable fillers (Swashbuckler) that only nudge a failing boss estimate, unless that joker alone lifts the next blind above about 80%. A swap must add a multiplier, a lasting chips source your deck triggers, or a scaler you will feed for several antes.
- Do not hold scalers that pull against each other on discards. Banner, Green Joker and Mystic Summit want zero discards; Castle and Ramen-style discard users want many. Pick one direction when you buy the second one, and sell or skip the one that conflicts.
- Do not play Straights or Flushes as filler once you have jokers for the main hand and no enabler. In a desperate last shop, do not switch to a hand you can't reliably draw: with 8 cards, 2 discards and no Four Fingers or Shortcut, a Straight in one hand is only about a 25-30% event. The empty-board case is the exception: see the in-blind pace rule.

From ante 2 to ante 5, while the board has fewer than 2 multiplier sources, spend all surplus above $25 in every shop. A suit-dependent xMult (Ancient x1.5, Bloodstone) counts as half, and as nothing on an even 13-per-suit deck playing Pairs unless the deck is already tilted toward that suit or you commit to tilting it with suit-converting tarots or Arcana packs. Lusty was sold for Bloodstone and the result was called 'the lasting multiplier', but the deck stayed at 13 Hearts and the next ante still read 10%/0%. Loyalty Card and other periodic xMult do not count: with 4 hands it fires about once every 1.5 rounds, and it may never fire against a boss like The Eye. Spending means 1-2 $5 rerolls spread across shops, Buffoon packs, and xMult or +Mult jokers. Start the hunt in earnest at ante 3, with Buffoon packs as well as rerolls, and keep the cash to buy the xMult when it appears. Do not spend the run's money on rerolls in a safe ante 2: one run's first Buffoon pack after ante 1 came at ante 5, its only xMult was a perishable Duo at ante 6, and it could not afford Blueprint. If the main hand is below its level target, buy its planet first. Once the hand is at target, more planets, planet infrastructure (Telescope, extra Celestial packs) and hand-boosting +Mult (Supernova) are not progress, so all surplus goes to rerolls and Buffoon packs for xMult until one reliable every-hand xMult is on the board. A run that rerolled only twice and put $38 into Pair levels kept seeing a cliff one ante ahead.
- Never pass a real xMult (The Idol, Cavendish, Card Sharp, Acrobat and similar) just to keep an interest tier while a slot is open, or because of a rental or eternal sticker (see the rentals rule). Empty slots never grow.
- With empty slots and money above $25 in antes 2-3, buy durable, non-rental scorers that fit the main hand (Raised Fist, Sly, Castle or Greedy when the deck feeds them). Do not pass them while waiting for an xMult. A full board buys time to find the multiplier and prevents panic rental buys at ante 4. If the next ante reads below 30%, a perishable or eternal scorer for the played hand also qualifies (see the unreliable-scoring rule); leaving 2-3 slots empty through ante 3 is a failure.
- If the board still has no xMult by ante 5, sell spent flat or economy jokers (Misprint, Gros Michel) early to fund the search, not after the money is gone.
- Do not swap one flat +Mult or chips joker for another as a fix. It only counts if the outlook rises.
- Joker Stencil is a stopgap: take any xMult, scaling or growing joker even if it lowers Stencil, and judge it by the score needed 1-2 antes ahead.
- Do not spend this surplus on Arcana, Spectral or Standard packs that add one-card tweaks, or on Golden Joker or other economy, unless you are aiming at a specific card the build needs.
- Spend a windfall of $20+ over target (Investment Tag, big interest, Hermit) this way before the Small Blind, spread across that ante's shops. Do not pour it into escalating rerolls in one shop.

Crisis cash discipline: when a blind or boss looks lost, every purchase must raise it clearly. That means about +10-15 points on the boss, or lifting a failing blind above about 50%. A buy that moves a doomed boss from 15% to 20% is not a fix (Sly 10→15%, Dusk 19%, sell-and-reroll 18%); keep the money for the next shop and the next ante.
- When a boss two or more blinds away reads below 30%, rank each possible buy by how much it raises that boss read per dollar. The Small and Big Blind shops are where the boss gets fixed, so look hardest there (a reroll or pack aimed at +Mult or xMult). Do not leave those shops at $6-8 and then dump $13 into the last shop before the boss, when it is too late to find anything better.
- When a boss you must beat is below 50%, spend at most about half your money on rerolls in one shop. Stop when the next reroll would leave under about $12 for the remaining shops before the boss. Each later shop is a fresh roll for xMult, and you need money there to buy the xMult plus a planet.
- While shops remain in the ante, never spend to $0. Keep at least the price of a common xMult ($6) plus $3 per rental due at round end, and about $5-8 for the last shop before the boss. Pick the cheaper scorer first, and carry out a planned sale of a non-scoring joker before the boss.
- Grabber, Observatory and other vouchers that do not reroll the boss, economy jokers (a perishable Business Card), random Arcana or Celestial packs, off-plan levels and sideways flat-joker swaps do not count as fixes. Never put the whole bankroll on a voucher that fixes the Big Blind but leaves the boss below 20%. Grabber for $10 at $11 took the Big Blind from 60% to 97% but The Arm only from 5% to 10%, and left $1 with nothing buyable. Director's Cut does count (see the boss rule). Once the next boss reads 10% or less, every dollar goes to rerolls, packs or planets aimed at a multiplier. Count a perishable or rental that expires this ante as already gone. Never spend your last money on a voucher and then skip a blind.
- When the final boss reads 15% or less, stop buying +5% steps, such as $3 off-plan planets just for Constellation's x0.1. Stop buy-then-sell trials too (Splash sold one decision later). Keep $10+ for the last two shops and spend it only on what can multiply the score: a reroll or Buffoon pack aimed at an xMult or big-chips joker, or a Mercury. Four Constellation planets and four empty rerolls took $26 to $0, and the final shops could not afford a single look.
- Flag the run as in trouble as soon as the outlook shows the next ante at 0-15%. React with targeted certain upgrades in the current ante (see the severe-forecast exception), not by emptying the bank in a panic.

Skipping blinds. A skip gives up the blind payout, the unused-hand money, an interest round and a whole shop. Rare, Uncommon, Holographic, Foil, Voucher, Coupon, Polychrome, Negative and money tags (Economy, Handy, Investment) pay out only after a later blind, so skipping sends you into the next blind with the same board.
- Do not skip in an ante where the boss is below about 40-50%, or where the boss estimate is likely optimistic (it rests on one conditional joker, an xMult that depends on drawing specific ranks, or a boss that debuffs cards or drains levels like The Head, The Goad or The Arm). Never skip the Big Blind when the boss after it reads under 50%: its payout and shop are the last chance to fix that boss. Skipping both ante 4 blinds into The Mouth for a Negative Tag gave about 2%, against about 5% for playing. Play the last blind before the boss if it is at least 60%, and use that shop to fix the board. Never skip both blinds of an ante into a boss below 50%. When you are broke (under about $10), play the blind for its shop and the unused-hand money.
- Skip a Small Blind only when the board reads about 100% through the next boss and money is at least $20, so the lost shop is not needed.
- While the board has no xMult and the next ante reads below about 30%, never skip for an economy tag (Investment included); every shop is a chance at the multiplier. Skipping ante 3's Big Blind for Investment broke the strategist's own 'no skips while collapsing' rule, and the $25 then went into empty rerolls. In that state, skip only for a tag that shows jokers or planets at once (Buffoon, Charm), and only if you will sell a joker to take what it offers.
- In antes 1-2, skip for an economy tag (Investment included, despite its reputation as the good ante 1 skip) only on a solid board: at least 2 lasting scorers, or 1 unconditional scorer plus a main-hand planet, and a boss reading 98%+. A 95% read carried by a lone suit joker (Wrathful) does not qualify. In antes 2-4, do not skip for a Meteor or other planet tag; the shop could show an xMult.
- Later, skip the pre-boss blind for a money tag only if the boss has read at least 90% for two or more shops in a row and the shop you give up has nothing you want.
- Never skip for a D6 or other reroll tag while the board lacks scoring, or while the next ante's boss reads low. The rerolls it gives are still a lottery; a D6 skip at ante 3 found nothing.
- Never skip for a joker tag (Rare, Uncommon, Buffoon, Mega Buffoon, Holographic, Foil) with all slots full unless you have already named a weak non-eternal joker to sell where it pays out. A Rare Tag taken with 5 full slots (one an eternal Riff-Raff) gave nothing and cost a payout and a shop at $9. A Mega Buffoon skip at ante 4 took nothing, though Green Joker was offered, because 'every slot is full'. In that shop or pack, always look at what is offered and sell the weakest or expiring joker (spent Seltzer, decaying Ice Cream, economy, flat filler) to take it if it scores better or adds a multiplier. When the run is struggling, skip only if the tag itself fixes the next blind.
- When a free pack opens (Meteor, Mega Celestial), always take something: main-hand or Pair planets first, otherwise a related hand's planet.

Eternal jokers are a permanent slot cost. Before any Eternal buy, ask: 'when the xMult shows up, which slot does it go in?'
- Before ante 5, lock at most one slot with a non-xMult Eternal, and only for a scaler or scorer that fits the main hand and does not fight the rest of the board. Mystic Summit wants zero discards and works against discard users. Riff-Raff needs empty slots. Never hold more than 2 non-xMult Eternals at any point. Never take an Eternal for a different hand type (Crafty for Flush on a Pair board).
- From ante 3, while the board has no xMult, keep at least one slot free or sellable for it. Buy no new non-xMult Eternal then (an Eternal Blue Joker filled the 5th slot, so every later find needed a sale). Never sell a key Mult source for an Eternal utility joker: Misprint was sold for an Eternal Astronomer before a Big Blind reading 30-38%, which added no score, and the Celestial pack it was meant to make free could not be bought.
- On a near-empty board (3+ free slots) with a failing forecast before ante4, the first Eternal scorer for the played hand costs little: do not turn it down for the sticker. Passing Devious, Campfire, Walkie Talkie and an $8 Supernova on sticker grounds while The Arm read 5%, then spending $10 on a voucher, lost the run.
- Never take an Eternal flat or conditional +Mult or chips joker, or an Eternal utility joker, if it would make 2+ Eternal slots. That holds even when it is free from a pack (Swashbuckler, Fibonacci, Supernova, Walkie Talkie). The only exception is a next blind below 50% without it, with nothing else that fixes it. Skip the pick instead: a locked slot is worth more than +4 Mult once you need room for xMult. Eternal is fine on a real xMult.
- From ante 3, and certainly by ante 5, keep at least 2 non-eternal slots you can sell or swap, so the convert-to-xMult step stays possible. Boards with 3-5 Eternal flat scorers could not add an xMult, because every swap lowered the outlook (selling the one free Green Joker dropped a 97% blind to 12%).
- If a blind forces a third Eternal, take the one with the highest ceiling (an xMult, Hanging Chad, a retrigger), not flat Mult. Never take an Eternal rental for flat Mult (see the rentals rule).
- In antes 1-2, do not lock a slot with an Eternal joker that is flat filler or will be a weak flat effect by ante 4 (Eternal plain Joker, Splash, Sly, Arrowhead, Fibonacci, Blue Joker). Take one only if the next blind is below 70% without it.
- When opening a Buffoon pack with no jokers, rank the choices by how many chips they add to an ordinary hand right now, and take a scorer if there is one. If the pack has no scorer, take nothing in antes 1-2 (see the survival rule): a free Drunkard became a crutch that Banner depended on. Later, with 4+ free slots, an economy joker is acceptable only if no scorer will come to depend on it and you sell it for the first scorer. Count it toward the Eternal cap.
- Do not buy a Buffoon pack, or skip for a Buffoon Tag, when every slot is full and the only sellable joker is a key scorer. Decide before paying what you would sell; otherwise spend on a planet or keep the interest.

Selling jokers, and outlook noise.
- Keep your xMult. Never sell a permanent xMult joker (Card Sharp, The Idol, Seeing Double, a permanent x3 Flower Pot, etc.) for a perishable or decaying joker (Turtle Bean, Popcorn, Ice Cream, Seltzer, Ramen), even if the sim says it fixes the current boss. Selling Seeing Double for Turtle Bean lifted one boss from 41% to 86%, but the Bean was worth $3 by ante 7 and ante 8 was played with a single xMult. Do not sell an xMult for a flat or scaling +Mult joker unless the boss you are about to face is impossible with it, and never for a joker that adds no score (Juggler, Splash, economy). If one boss needs a fix, sell a flat, expiring or rental joker, or spend money. From ante 6, the count of permanent xMult jokers should only go up (target 2+ by ante 7). Be suspicious of a short-term outlook jump from a hand-size joker when the next ante needs a multiplier. Before any swap that removes a multiplier, compare the next ante's outlook with and without the swap, not just the next blind's. $3 a round in rent for an x3 is cheap, and one reliable xMult is worth about +2.5 blinds.
- Convert flat to multiplier when the cliff is near. If the outlook shows a boss within the next ante at 10% or less and the board has no xMult, stop guarding a current blind that reads 95%+. Sell the weakest flat joker for any xMult or scaling joker (Blackboard, Ride the Bus, Green Joker, Hanging Chad, Obelisk) as long as the current blind still reads about 75%+ after the swap. Keeping the flat board means losing at the next ante for sure: refusing Hanging Chad, Obelisk, Blackboard (the only xMult offered all run) and Ride the Bus to protect The Hook at 97% lost the run, with ante 5 reading 0-15% the whole time.
- Do not sell a working, still-growing +Mult joker for a trigger xMult (Loyalty Card and other every-N-hands jokers) unless it fires on most boss attempts. Divide N by the hands you actually play per round: if it fires less than about once every two rounds, it is not a multiplier for planning. Red Card at +9 sold for Loyalty left ante 5 reading 10%/0%, and Loyalty was sold six decisions later.
- In the last shop before a blind, never sell a scoring joker for another flat or conditional joker, or to nudge a later boss, if that blind's read goes down, unless it still reads 95%+ afterward. (The xMult conversion above is the exception, with its 75% floor.) Abstract Joker loses +3 Mult for every joker sold. A boss estimate means nothing if you die on the blind before it: selling Banner to lift the boss from 52% to 59% dropped a 100% Small Blind to 51%, and the run lost that blind.
- Treat outlook changes under about 10 points as noise (boss reads swing 40-65% from shop to shop on an unchanged board). Never trade a known, lasting effect (a joker, a slot, a blind's payout) for a small simulated gain.
- Conditional xMult like Flower Pot is still a bonus, not the engine. It checks only scoring cards, so a kicker never helps. Two Pair covers all four suits only about 1 time in 6, and Full House about half the time. Do not pick the main hand around it, and do not accept an outlook that depends on it firing. When it struggles against one boss, change how you play (five-card hands that cover all four suits, Wild cards) rather than selling it.
- If your only xMult needs a hand that is hard to draw with 2 discards (The Trio, The Family, Four of a Kind), shape the deck at once with Strength, Death or Hanged Man to pile cards onto a few ranks. Keep the scorer for the hand you actually draw most (do not sell the Mad Joker powering Two Pair) until the deck can make the target hand. Otherwise stay on Pair.

Score the build against the actual boss, and keep a way to change bosses.
- Once the boss is shown, rate every shop of the ante against its rule, not against the Small or Big Blind. For a one-hand boss like The Needle, only per-hand +Mult, xMult and main-hand planets count. Skip delayed or counter jokers (Loyalty Card, Ride the Bus, Runner, Wee, Lucky Cat) and economy until the one-hand score clears. A boss debuff (e.g. The Goad on Spades) applies only to the boss, so play normally in the Small and Big Blinds.
- Against The Arm, never play the levelled main hand. Before the round, name one off-plan sacrifice hand (High Card or a spare hand), lock the round player to it (override Card Sharp/Burglar 'repeat the hand' logic), and clear in as few hands as you can. Hold main-hand planets and any Fool until after The Arm. Playing Pair into The Arm took it from level 6 to level 2.
- Director's Cut: from ante 4, if it is in the shop and you have $10 above your interest floor, buy it before any reroll or pack. This matters most when the current boss or the next ante's boss reads below 50%, or when the engine has a boss it cannot beat (Card Sharp or Burglar repeat plans against The Eye, The Arm, The Psychic). Get it by ante 5-6 at the latest. A boss reroll is a lasting fix; $10 of rerolls is a gamble. Leaving it in the shop for 6 decisions with $31-50 in hand led to death against a 29-40% Pillar. But it fixes only a bad boss. If the next ante's ordinary blinds (Small or Big) read below about 50% and the board has no lasting xMult, a boss reroll fixes nothing. Put that $10 into xMult hunting (Buffoon packs, rerolls) or main-hand planets first, and buy Director's Cut once the board can beat ordinary blinds. A $10 Director's Cut bought at the run's peak of $37, with ante 4 reading 0-5%, was never used, and later $10 rolls were unaffordable.
- Buy other vouchers only if they work with the engine you already have. Observatory is dead money with Constellation, because planets are used at once instead of held. Hieroglyph and Petroglyph are not worth draining the bank to $15.
- In any round rated below about 95%, turn off grow_joker style goals and play the highest score each hand. Grow scalers only on blinds that are about 100% safe. Do not buy fresh slow scalers (Square, Wee, Runner) at ante 3+ unless they can be fed for free.

In-blind pace rule: play each blind to its chip target.
- Before every hand, work out chips still needed ÷ hands left (a 300 blind over 4 hands needs 75 per hand). If the best hand you can play now won't keep that pace, discard toward a bigger hand while discards remain, even if that breaks a pair you already hold.
- With only 2 discards at Gold, use them early, while 3-4 hands remain to play what they dig up.
- On a blank board (no jokers, every hand at level 1), Pair is not the plan. A level-1 Pair scores about 30-64 and Two Pair about 60-80, both below pace. Dig for Three of a Kind (about 100-180), a Straight (about 200-260) or a Flush (about 250-300). Play a lone Pair or High Card only when it keeps pace or finishes the blind as the last hand.
- If the score after hand 2 is below 50% of the target, switch to the highest-variance line available (discard toward a Flush or Straight).
- Treat losing a blind rated 90%+ as a play error and audit it. Log every hand and discard as its own decision: cards, expected score, running total, chips still needed, hands and discards left.
